findings.reason: the verb's refusal must be the complement of §2's prefix rule ("recorded head begins with the dispatched head"); as written it targets the wrong rows and, applied by §4, destroys genuine reviews instead of correcting misattributed ones.
findings.text: the verb "refuses a row whose recorded head is the dispatched head" (equality, repeated in the done-when at line 84), while §2 defines a row as mismatched when its recorded head "does not begin with" the dispatched head and its own negative control certifies nova's r-20261018T172216624608-review-of-vertical-pin-45213bf1cd62 — dispatched head taken from the 12-hex node-id suffix, recorded head `45213bf1cd6216df…` — as correctly attributed; under equality that row is not refused, so `repair-review` appends a correction to a row whose review is sound and §4 applies it across every mounted ledger

findings.reason: naming the argument (`carried_revision_pair(row["review"])`) is the difference between the verb refusing a correctly-attributed row and correcting it, the same corruption the prefix finding describes.
findings.text: the verb is said to read "the recorded head through `carried_revision_pair`" without saying the argument is the row's `review` block, but a ledger row carries the head nested (`row["review"]["reviewed_head_sha"]`, verified on docs/state/reckon/runs/*.json; the row's top level has no `reviewed_head_sha`), and `carried_revision_pair` reads only the mapping it is handed, so a literal `carried_revision_pair(row)` finds no recorded head and the "recorded head is the dispatched head" refusal never fires
